branches.title: Philosophy
branches.summary: Philosophy maps for lineages, schools, methods, texts, and recurring problems.

maps.title: Metaphysics families
maps.subtitle: A review draft for Metaphysics families.
maps.question: What are the major families inside metaphysics families, and what problem does each one solve?
maps.summary: A generated review draft of major metaphysical families, their central claims, pressure points, contributors, texts, and relations.

groups.title: Physicalism and materialism
groups.stance: Reality is ultimately physical, and minds, values, causes, and social facts must fit inside the natural order.
groups.centralClaim: Everything real is either physical or depends on physical reality in a disciplined way.
groups.whyItMatters: This is the default pressure behind much current science, philosophy of mind, and secular metaphysics.

contributors.name: Thomas Hobbes
contributors.reason: Treats thought, sensation, and politics through bodies in motion rather than immaterial substances.

contributors.name: J. J. C. Smart
contributors.reason: Gives a clean modern argument that sensations can be identical with brain processes.

contributors.name: David Armstrong
contributors.reason: Builds a systematic materialist account of mind, properties, and laws.

texts.title: A Materialist Theory of the Mind
A World of States of Affairs

objections: Conscious experience can look underexplained if physical description leaves out what it is like.
Norms, meanings, numbers, and possibilities may not reduce neatly to physical facts.

groups.title: Idealism
groups.stance: Mind, experience, concepts, or spirit are not late accidents inside reality; they are basic to how reality is intelligible.
groups.centralClaim: Reality is dependent on, structured by, or inseparable from mind-like activity.
groups.whyItMatters: Idealism keeps forcing the question of whether a world without experience is even thinkable as a world.

contributors.name: George Berkeley
contributors.reason: Argues that ordinary objects are collections of ideas sustained by perception.

texts.title: A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge
Three Dialogues between Hylas and Philonous

contributors.name: Immanuel Kant
contributors.reason: Moves the debate toward the conditions that make experience and objecthood possible.

contributors.name: G. W. F. Hegel
contributors.reason: Treats reality as historically and logically articulated through self-developing reason.

objections: It can seem to dissolve independent reality into the conditions of knowing.
It risks becoming too large and elastic to test against ordinary experience.

groups.title: Dualism
groups.stance: Reality contains a deep distinction between mind and matter, form and body, or soul and world.
groups.centralClaim: Mental reality cannot be fully captured by physical substance alone.
groups.whyItMatters: Dualism makes the mind-body problem explicit instead of hiding it inside a single substance vocabulary.

contributors.name: Plato
contributors.reason: Separates changing sensible things from more stable intelligible forms and soul.

contributors.name: Rene Descartes
contributors.reason: Frames the modern mind-body problem with thinking substance and extended substance.

contributors.name: Elisabeth of Bohemia
contributors.reason: Presses Descartes on how an immaterial mind could move a material body.

objections: Explaining interaction between unlike substances is notoriously difficult.
Modern neuroscience pressures any account that treats mind as cleanly separable from body.

groups.title: Substance metaphysics and hylomorphism
groups.stance: Things are structured substances: matter is organized by form, powers, purposes, categories, and persistence conditions.
groups.centralClaim: To understand reality, ask what kinds of things exist, what makes them one thing, and what lets them persist through change.
groups.whyItMatters: This tradition supplies the grammar behind categories, essences, organisms, artifacts, and personhood.

contributors.name: Aristotle
contributors.reason: Explains beings through substance, form, matter, potentiality, and actuality.

contributors.name: Thomas Aquinas
contributors.reason: Connects Aristotelian substance and form with theology, causation, and being.

contributors.name: E. J. Lowe
contributors.reason: Revives categories, substances, and dependence in contemporary analytic metaphysics.

objections: Essences can look too rigid for evolution, history, and social construction.
The language of form and substance can seem outdated next to field, process, and system models.

groups.title: Process metaphysics
groups.stance: Reality is better understood as activity, event, relation, change, and becoming than as static things with fixed essences.
groups.centralClaim: Processes are primary, and stable objects are patterns inside ongoing activity.
groups.whyItMatters: Process thought fits naturally with evolution, ecology, systems theory, and time-centered accounts of reality.

contributors.name: Heraclitus
contributors.reason: Makes change, tension, and logos central to understanding reality.

contributors.name: Alfred North Whitehead
contributors.reason: Rebuilds metaphysics around events, occasions, relations, and creativity.

contributors.name: Henri Bergson
contributors.reason: Treats lived time and creative evolution as basic rather than derivative.

objections: If everything is process, it can be hard to explain identity and stable reference.
Technical process systems can become obscure without clear examples.

groups.title: Neutral monism and panpsychism
groups.stance: The mental and physical may be two aspects, organizations, or expressions of something more basic.
groups.centralClaim: Mind and matter do not have to be rival substances if both arise from a deeper neutral or experiential ground.
groups.whyItMatters: This family is a recurring escape route from both reductionist physicalism and interactionist dualism.

contributors.name: Baruch Spinoza
contributors.reason: Treats mind and body as attributes of one underlying substance.

contributors.name: Bertrand Russell
contributors.reason: Opens a route where physics describes structure while intrinsic nature may be experience-like.

contributors.name: William James
contributors.reason: Treats pure experience as more basic than the later split between subject and object.

contributors.name: Galen Strawson
contributors.reason: Argues that experience is a real feature of the physical rather than an alien addition.

objections: The combination problem asks how tiny experiential units compose unified minds.
Neutral stuff can become mysterious if it is neither clearly mental nor clearly physical.

groups.title: Pragmatism and metaphysical critique
groups.stance: Metaphysical claims should be judged by the work they do in inquiry, life, language, and practice.
groups.centralClaim: Some metaphysical debates are clarified, redirected, or dissolved when we ask what difference they make.
groups.whyItMatters: This family keeps Atlas maps honest by asking when a grand theory actually improves understanding.

contributors.name: Charles Sanders Peirce
contributors.reason: Links meaning to conceivable practical effects while keeping truth tied to inquiry.

texts.title: How to Make Our Ideas Clear

contributors.name: William James
contributors.reason: Turns metaphysical disagreement toward lived consequences and temperaments.

contributors.name: John Dewey
contributors.reason: Treats experience, nature, and inquiry as continuous rather than split into metaphysical compartments.

contributors.name: Rudolf Carnap
contributors.reason: Challenges metaphysics when its sentences lack clear empirical or logical role.

texts.title: The Elimination of Metaphysics Through Logical Analysis of Language

objections: Critique can become too deflationary and miss real ontological disagreement.
Practical consequences may not decide what reality is like.

relations.note: These families often begin from opposite intuitions, so their contrast is useful for review.
The second position answers a pressure point exposed by the first.
The later bridge reframes the earlier conflict instead of simply choosing a side.
The process or revisionary view shifts attention from stable categories to change and use.
Both positions treat practice, time, or inquiry as central to metaphysical judgment.
The bridge position borrows from the mind-first family while resisting a full idealist collapse.
